description.value: The whole of what was left on a lee ledge after a division: two worked crevice tools, a quantity of shed plate and a broken hammerstone, lifted as a group in 2258 and kept as one. Nothing here was taken away by the two who walked back up the crest, which is the rule rather than an oversight, so the scatter is a complete assemblage of a kind that is normally impossible to obtain. The plate is from one body and the tools are from two, and that observation settled a long argument about whether tools are held before division. Every piece is water-worn, it having rained on the ledge for the six years between the division and the collection.

notes.value: Collected under Protocol 1 as material in a public setting, on the argument that a ledge nobody ever returns to is not a dwelling. The argument has been contested twice and upheld twice.
